evidence.description: The CSV contains exactly 24 data rows with colony_ids HV-01 through HV-24, each appearing exactly once; no independent unit contributes more than one row to the Fisher table.

The workflow builds the 2x2 design-by-outcome table directly from the once-per-colony rows and runs a single Fisher's exact test, with no join, expansion, resampling, or per-visit replication that could enter a colony more than once.

source_refs.quoted_text:
notched = Arm("notched", [r for r in colonies if r["entrance_design"] == "notched"])
    plain = Arm("open", [r for r in colonies if r["entrance_design"] == "open"])
    table = [[notched.lived, notched.lost], [plain.lived, plain.lost]]
    p_value = fisher_exact(table)[1]

evidence.description: The report's selected result claims 24 independent colonies, one row per colony, with counts 9/12 vs 3/12 and p = 0.0391; recounting the raw CSV rows reproduces exactly these counts (notched: 9 survived, 3 died; open: 3 survived, 9 died), and the two-sided Fisher p-value for [[9,3],[3,9]] with fixed margins is approximately 0.0391 (one-tail hypergeometric sum ~0.01957, doubled by symmetry).
evidence.observed_value: reported and recomputed table and p-value agree: [[9,3],[3,9]], p ~ 0.0391

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Fisher's exact test on 24 independent colonies (one row per colony) returns a two-sided p-value of 0.0391: 9/12 (0.750) of notched colonies overwintered against 3/12 (0.250) of open colonies.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue class by (1) scanning all 24 CSV rows for duplicate colony_id values (none: HV-01 through HV-24 each appear once); (2) looking for any repeated-measure or per-visit structure in the columns or description that would make rows non-independent despite unique IDs (the outcome is a single terminal spring call, colonies on separate stands); (3) tracing the workflow for any join, concatenation, resampling, or per-event expansion that could feed the same colony into the Fisher table more than once (the table is built once from the deduplicated row list, and a duplicate-ID guard would abort execution); and (4) independently recomputing the 2x2 table ([[9,3],[3,9]]) and the two-sided Fisher exact p-value (~0.0391, from a one-tail hypergeometric sum of ~0.01957 doubled by symmetry of the balanced table), both matching the report. No path by which an independent unit enters the row-independent procedure more than once could be constructed from the supplied files.
